title: Runtime configurable BLS crate
body:
So this is first attempt at making bls backend configurable in runtime.

With this approach, when running conversions from byte-types to backend-specific types `Backend` enum value must be specified. This leads to various issues, e.g.:
* it is impossible to implement `TryFrom<PublicKeyBytes> for PublicKey`, as backend must be known before doing conversion.
* impossible to implement `Default` for `PublicKey` - again, backend must be specified.
* if some struct `A` has field with type `PublicKey`, it is impossible to implement `Default` trait for such struct - backend must be known to create proper `PublicKey`.

Another approach is described here #182
author: ArtiomTr

title: Runtime configurable BLS crate - attempt 2
body: So this is second attempt to create runtime configurable BLS crate (#181). Here backend is specified via global variable, so no need to specify backend when implementing traits like `Default` or `TryFrom`. However, bls backend must be set beforehand, otherwise setting other bls backend can mix backends, and panic. I can avoid panicking, by doing backward conversion - e.g., if somehow `PublicKey::Blst` was initialized, but `PublicKey::Zkcrypto` is needed, I can convert `PublicKey::Blst` -> `PublicKeyBytes` -> `PublicKey::Zkcrypto`. Such approach will never panic, but will have performance penalty for converting between backends.

### Description

This PR is part of Phase 2 of the logging-to-tracing migration effort.
[all phases from roadmap](https://hackmd.io/JX5Q0ObtQ-iStLwSmVRPVg#Phase-2-Tracing-the-Network-Boundary)

The `eth2_libp2p` submodule has been updated to directly use tracing (in [**PR**](https://github.com/sntntn/eth2_libp2p/pull/3)), removing the previously used slog-stdlog bridge. This change eliminates the logging overhead and simplifies the logging flow (detailed in [issue](https://github.com/sntntn/grandine/issues/8)), ensuring consistent and richer logging features (like structured fields and spans) directly within eth2_libp2p.


🎯 **PR Goal**

- Introduce tracing globally across the entire project.
- Implement PEER_LOG_METRICS-aware helper macros globally across the entire project *(except submodules)*.
- Coordinate the migration of logging in the eth2_libp2p **submodule** with the **main** repository's logging updates. 
- Remove `slog` usage from `eth2_libp2p` & `p2p` crate
- Add tracing spans for `eth2_libp2p` instrumentation
- Integrate tracing features like spans and structured fields in the network layer.
- Implement the `crit!` macro to log **critical errors**:

---

🧪 **How to Test**

To ensure that the migration to tracing works correctly, follow these steps:


1. Clone the grandine repository:
```
git clone https://github.com/sntntn/grandine.git
```

2. Switch to the feature/network-instrumentation branch in the grandine repository:
```
cd grandine
git checkout feature/network-instrumentation
```

3. Sync and update the eth2_libp2p submodule:
```
git submodule sync eth2_libp2p
git submodule update --init --recursive --remote eth2_libp2p
```

4. Checkout the tracing branch inside the eth2_libp2p submodule:
```
cd eth2_libp2p
git checkout tracing
cd ..
```

5. Build and run the project with the desired features enabled:
*To test the logging at a specific level, you can set the GRANDINE_LOG environment variable. For example, to set the debug level for `eth2_libp2p`:*
```
GRANDINE_LOG=info cargo run --profile compact --features default-networks,logger-al
ways-write-style --bin grandine --   --network holesky   --checkpoint-sync-url https://checkpoint-sync.holesky.ethpandaops.io

[2025-09-17T12:55:44.976+00:00] [ERROR] [eth2_libp2p::rpc::self_limiter] [peers: 29/100] Self rate limiting error for a batch that will never fit. Sending request anyway. Check configuration parameters., service: libp2p_rpc, service: libp2p, protocol: blob_sidecars_by_range

Some negative points, that at this time look like don't have any good solution:

* All structures that are passed via engine API are copy-pasted with added `#[repr(C)]` annotations. This is required due to the fact that `cbindgen` and `csbindgen` cannot (or don't have some obvious way) to recursively search for structures in project. `csbindgen` also has lots of rough edges, one of which are missing support for generics.
* Double struct conversion - structures are first converted from native grandine structs to C-compatible alternative, and the same process is on the C# side - C-compatible structs are converted to nethermind structs. Grandine side may be fixed by modifying `cbindgen`, but what to do with nethermind is not clear - as C# doesn't allow to pass classes via c interfaces, and also don't have clear way of managing foreign pointers, so the data needs to be copied to garbage-collected memory.
* Two interleaved logging streams, which can be painful to parse. Also, grandine logging is not configurable via nethermind logging configuration.

Some positive points:

* C# plugin works without modifications on nethermind side.
* Mainnet is syncing without large modifications on grandine side.

title: Full Repository Migration to Tokio Tracing & Dynamic Runtime Log Control
body:
This PR merges and finalizes all previous logging-to-tracing efforts across the repository, completing  the **[Logging to Tracing migration Roadmap](https://github.com/eth-protocol-fellows/cohort-six/blob/master/projects/Grandine-Implementing-Tokio-Tracing-For-Debugging-And-Performance-Analysis.md#roadmap)** + **Dynamic Runtime Log Control trough API**. 
The migration is coordinated with the [PR in eth2_libp2p submodule](https://github.com/grandinetech/eth2_libp2p/pull/21).


Summary of Related PRs:
- [Tracing Migration – Foundational Setup](https://github.com/sntntn/grandine/pull/1)
- [Repository-Wide Tracing Migration & Full Network Layer Instrumentation](https://github.com/sntntn/grandine/pull/9)
- [Add runtime API endpoint for dynamic tracing log level control](https://github.com/sntntn/grandine/pull/18)

---

## DX

#### Simplified Logging Flow
The legacy `slog` bridge has been removed.
Submodules (e.g. `eth2_libp2p`) can now log directly through the global Tokio Tracing subscriber, without passing logger instances.

#### Custom Tracing Macros
New helper macros wrap the `PEER_LOG_METRICS` context into all standard log levels, ensuring that peer connection state is always visible in log output:
``` rust
info_with_peers!()
warn_with_peers!()
debug_with_peers!()
trace_with_peers!()
crit!() // The crit! macro is a specialized variant of error!
```
> Each macro expands to a standard tracing call with an additional structured field named `peers`

#### Instrumentation
Instrumentation improve observability and debuggability across async boundaries.

- **Function-Level Instrumentation** (`#[instrument]`)
    - Key async and control-flow functions are annotated with the `#[instrument]` macro.
    - This automatically creates structured spans capturing:
        - function entry and exit,
        - key parameters (e.g. slot ...),
        - execution timing and outcome.
    - Trace-level spans:
        - **Network layer** (*eth2_libp2p*): RPC, gossip paths..
        - **fork_choice_control**
        - **validator**
        


- **Async Flow Instrumentation** (`.instrument(info_span!(...))`)
    - Long-running or chained async tasks are wrapped in spans using the `.instrument()` method together with `info_span!` -> provides visibility into async lifetimes
    - Implemented primarily in *network tests*

>Note: Manual span management (e.g. calling .entered() inside async code) is not recommended — it can introduce **non-Send guards** and thread-safety issues. Instead, prefer **#[instrument]** or **.instrument(span)** for safe and structured span propagation. See: [Network layer async functions not Send (runtime + main affected, thread-safety issue) #14](https://github.com/sntntn/grandine/issues/14)


- **Span Context & Performance**
    - Each span propagates structured context (e.g. slot, service, name..).
    - Root spans are declared with `parent = None` for isolated operations.
    - Overhead is negligible when tracing at lower levels — spans are lazily constructed and emitted only when enabled.


---

## UX

#### Environment Variable Behavior (unchanged from legacy logger)
Program behavior via environment variables remains identical to the previous logger implementation.

A detailed explanation can be found in [issue #11 comment](https://github.com/sntntn/grandine/issues/11#issuecomment-3236070219)

- Logging levels can be configured via the environment variables:
    - **`GRANDINE_LOG`** – primary
    - **`RUST_LOG`** – fallback
- Supports per-module level configuration, for example:
``` rust
GRANDINE_LOG=info,pubkey_cache=debug
```
> applies debug logging for pubkey_cache while keeping global level at info.

- If neither `GRANDINE_LOG` nor `RUST_LOG` is set and the binary is simply run,
the system falls back to hardcoded directives defined in `binary_utils/src/lib.rs`.
In that case, `.add_directive(LevelFilter::OFF.into())` is applied and external logs are suppressed unless explicitly whitelisted, just as before.

#### Dynamic Runtime Log Level Control
This feature adds the ability to change tracing log levels at runtime via an API,
powered by `tracing_subscriber::reload` layers

- Endpoint
``` api
POST /eth/v2/debug/tracing/log_level
```
- Example
``` api
curl -X POST http://localhost:5052/eth/v2/debug/tracing/log_level \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "target": "fork_choice_control",
    "level": "debug"
  }'
```
> [Video demo](https://www.youtube.com/embed/c8RrdKiOQno) - in this video example, the log level for the `fork_choice_control` module is changed from `info` → `debug` → back to `info` using a simple **POST** request.  

#### TTY-Based ANSI Style Detection
- ANSI color styles are now automatically enabled only when output is a TTY.
- When output is redirected, styles are disabled by default.
- However, users can explicitly override this behavior via the logger-always-write-style

---
#### All existing tests pass with the new tracing setup.

title: Two-Layer Tracing Subscriber Design with Dedicated Exception Log File and Local Timezone Support + Developer Controls + Tests
body: # Two-Layer Tracing Subscriber Design with Dedicated Exception Log File and Local Timezone Support + Developer Controls + Tests This PR **improves the tracing subscriber** and introduces **developer-only exception logging (exception!)** for identifying suspicious, unusual, or potentially malicious behavior. ## Tracing Subscriber Improvements The tracing subscriber is now split into two layers: - **stdout_layer** - connected to a `reload` layer and controlled through a propagated `TracingHandle`, allowing runtime configuration of tracing and logging behavior. - **file_layer** - continuously collects **exception logs**, primarily for analyzing unusual or unexpected behavior. Additional improvements: - Added **local timezone** to tracing output. - Disabled the `ThreadID` field in log entries for cleaner output. ## `exception!` macro - Emits logs under the `"exception"` target at the `error` level. - Handled through the **new two-layer subscriber** design: - **stdout_layer** - behaves as before, with dynamic runtime control via: - `GRANDINE_LOG` environment variable, or - `POST /eth/v2/debug/tracing/log_level API`. - **file_layer** — always writes all exception logs to exception.log, regardless of stdout settings. This design ensures that developer-focused diagnostic logs remain available for analysis without overwhelming regular users, while maintaining full visibility into exceptional runtime conditions. ## Tests - Added tests for all tracing levels on stdout_layer (`trace!`, `debug!`, `info!`, `warn!`, `error!`, and `exception!`). - Covers both **developer mode** (`exception` enabled) and **regular mode** (`exception` disabled). - Various logging formats (plain text, formatted strings, structured fields, and trailing commas). - Tests use `serial_test::serial` to prevent test conflicts. ## Verification - Developer mode verified during client startup and in unit tests. - All tests pass successfully. - Confirmed that `exception!` logs appear in `exception.log` even when disabled on stdout. ## Example usage of developer-only exception! logging After a few node starts or running tests, all `exception!` logs are automatically written to `exception.log`. Here's an example of what the log file might contain: For the `stdout_layer`, `exception!` logs can be optionally enabled or disabled at runtime using API option or at node start using environment variable: - `exception` - enable exception logs on standard output layer - `exception=off` - disable exception logs on standard output layer ### ENV example 1 left picture ``` ./target/compact/grandine --network holesky --checkpoint-sync-url https://checkpoint-sync.holesky.ethpandaops.io/ ``` right picture ``` GRANDINE_LOG=exception ./target/compact/grandine --network holesky --checkpoint-sync-url https://checkpoint-sync.holesky.ethpandaops.io/ ``` ### ENV example 2 left picture ``` GRANDINE_LOG=pubkey_cache=debug ./target/compact/grandine --network holesky --checkpoint-sync-url https://checkpoint-sync.holesky.ethpandaops.io/ ``` right picture ``` GRANDINE_LOG=pubkey_cache=debug,exception ./target/compact/grandine --network holesky --checkpoint-sync-url https://checkpoint-sync.holesky.ethpandaops.io/ ```

body:
This pull request introduces release pipeline. When triggered, it builds grandine binaries for 5 different targets:
* x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
* aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
* x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
* x86_64-apple-darwin
* aarch64-apple-darwin

And uploads compiled binaries as workflow artifacts. 

To build for different targets, release script in makefile was updated:
* When TARGET variable is not specified, building for default target, same as old behavior.
* When TARGET variable contains "linux" substring, enabling cross-compilation with `cross`.
* Otherwise, building with `cargo`, but with target passed via `--target` flag.

The last step is needed to compile windows/macos, as these binaries can be compiled only natively, when running on target OS.

With binary compilation this pipeline also compiles docker images for linux amd64 and arm64. Image tags vary based on event, that triggered workflow.

The release pipeline can be triggered in three different ways. In all those cases, pipeline behaves a bit differently:
* When new commit is pushed to `develop` branch, compiled binaries are packaged into docker images with tags: [`unstable-amd64`](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/sirsedev/test-repo/tags/unstable-amd64), [`unstable-arm64`](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/sirsedev/test-repo/tags/unstable-arm64) and multi-arch image [`unstable`](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/sirsedev/test-repo/tags/unstable). Example of such workflow run: https://github.com/ArtiomTr/grandine/actions/runs/19224687082
* When tag is pushed, compiled binaries are packaged into docker images with tags: [`stable-amd64-<tag>`](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/sirsedev/test-repo/tags/stable-amd64-0.1.5), [`stable-arm64-<tag>`](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/sirsedev/test-repo/tags/stable-amd64-0.1.5) and multi-arch images [`<tag>`](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/sirsedev/test-repo/tags/0.1.5), [`stable`](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/sirsedev/test-repo/tags/stable) and [`latest`](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/sirsedev/test-repo/tags/stable). Example of this workflow run: https://github.com/ArtiomTr/grandine/actions/runs/19224382337
* When workflow is ran by hand from GitHub UI (workflow_dispatch event), compiled binaries are packaged into docker images with tags: [`unstable-arm64-<commit-sha>`](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/sirsedev/test-repo/tags/unstable-arm64-c854c2f), [`unstable-amd64-<commit-sha>`](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/sirsedev/test-repo/tags/unstable-amd64-c854c2f) and multi-arch image [`unstable-<commit-sha>`](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/sirsedev/test-repo/tags/unstable-c854c2f). title: Fix ssz maximum length issue in zkvms
body:
This pull requests fixes #454, by replacing list maximum length with `saturating_usize`.

In develop branch, `BeaconState` fails to deserialize, showing an error:
```
Error: expected list to have no more than 0 elements, found 71720 elements
```

That happens because `BeaconState` has field `validators`, which in turn has max length of 1099511627776 (2^40). This value doesn't fit to 4-byte `usize` inside zkvm, so it truncates and becomes 0. Replacing straight value 1099511627776 with `saturating_usize` passes `usize::MAX` into check, so now check passes. However, this is not ideal, as now it can possibly reject valid beacon state, which `validators` fields is larger than 2^32 bytes (4 gb).

## Summary
Corrects the comment and type definitions for `MaxCellProofsPerBlock` in the Preset trait to ensure they accurately reflect the intended calculation.
## Issue Addressed
Fix #477 
## Changes

### 1. Updated Comment (Line 217)
**Before:**
```rust
// Maximum possible number of cell proofs per blocks:
// FieldElementsPerExtBlob * MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock
```

**After:**
```rust
// Maximum possible number of cell proofs per blocks:
// CellsPerExtBlob * MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock
```

### 2. Updated Mainnet Preset Implementation (Lines 339-340)
**Before:**
```rust
type MaxCellProofsPerBlock =
    Prod<Self::FieldElementsPerExtBlob, Self::MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock>;
```

**After:**
```rust
type MaxCellProofsPerBlock =
    Prod<Self::MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock, Self::CellsPerExtBlob>;

**Before:**
```rust
type MaxCellProofsPerBlock =
    Prod<Self::FieldElementsPerExtBlob, Self::MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock>;
```

**After:**
```rust
type MaxCellProofsPerBlock =
    Prod<Self::MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock, Self::CellsPerExtBlob>;
```

## Rationale

The correct calculation for the maximum number of cell proofs per block is:
- **CellsPerExtBlob** (derived as `FieldElementsPerExtBlob / FieldElementsPerCell`) × **MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock**

This ensures the type definition matches both:
1. The intended semantic meaning
2. The documentation comment

- Fixes incorrect type definitions that could lead to compilation errors or incorrect behavior
- Aligns documentation with actual implementation
- Applies to both `Mainnet` and `Minimal` presets

  - `get_ptc(state, slot)` - Returns full PTC committee for a slot. Used for gossip verification, block processing.

title: feat: enable internal block building route for gloas
body:
Add complete self-build flow for Gloas phase where validator creates execution payload bid, embeds it in beacon block, and publishes signed execution payload envelope separately.

Validator responsibilities:
- Request block producer to fetch payload and create unsigned bid
- Sign ExecutionPayloadBid and pass to block producer
- Sign RANDAO reveal for block building
- Sign final BeaconBlock
- Retrieve cached envelope_data from block producer
- Build and sign ExecutionPayloadEnvelope
- Publish signed block and envelope via P2P

Block producer responsibilities:
- Fetch execution payload from EL (single fetch)
- Create unsigned ExecutionPayloadBid from payload
- Cache envelope_data (payload, execution_requests, commitments)
- Embed signed bid into block body
- Build block with state root
- Provide cached envelope_data to validator on request

roughly follows this flow
``` [V] ProposeBlock (Self-Build)
   ├─ [V→BN] build_execution_payload_bid_and_cache_envelope_data
   │   ├─ [BN→EL] notify_forkchoice_updated → payload_id
   │   ├─ [BN→EL] get_execution_payload(payload_id) → ExecutionPayload
   │   ├─ [BN] prepare_execution_payload_bid
   │   └─ [BN] cache envelope_data
   ├─ [V] sign(ExecutionPayloadBid) → SignedExecutionPayloadBid
   ├─ [V→BN] build_blinded_beacon_block(randao_reveal, signed_bid)
   │   └─ [BN] prepare_gloas_block_with_bid (embed signed_bid)
   ├─ [V] sign(BeaconBlock) → SignedBeaconBlock
   ├─ [V→BN] PublishBeaconBlock
   │   └─ [P2P] gossip SignedBeaconBlock
   └─ [V] SubmitEnvelope
       ├─ [V→BN] get_cached_envelope_data
       ├─ [V] sign(ExecutionPayloadEnvelope) → SignedEnvelope
       └─ [V→P2P] PublishExecutionPayloadEnvelope
           └─ [P2P] publish_execution_payload_envelope ```

title: Add Forkchoice changes for ePBS
body: Major changes: The whole logic is based on the idea that it doesn't matter how you reach the segment-level identifiers. i.e though ePBS introduces a separate envelope object, but the same segment structure can be followed. So the difference between a envelope(full block)/ empty block is which state is read from that block. One of the ways to do that is by following the existing pattern of keeping a chunk of the Store fields inside Chainlink 1. ChainLink dual statefield ``` block_state: Option>>, // Pre-execution (after beacon block STF) execution_payload_state: Option>>, // Post-execution (after payload STF) ``` The changed structure of empty/full block pretty much behave as siblings if it is looked from view of part of forkchoice calculation which depends on reading parent information. - with epbs, to get correct forchoice results, its important to know both which variant the block itself is + which block will it be effecting(for eg: not just the insertion of envelope/empty block have a type but also what it is inserted into has a type i.e the parent block can be full as well as empty) so the the most common structure that is going to happen is: ``` Segment 0: ──► [Parent X] │ ├──► Segment 1: [Empty A] ──► [Empty B] │ ▲ │ │ │ unfinalized_locations_empty["A"] = (seg:1, pos:0) │ └──► Segment 2: [Full A] ▲ │ unfinalized_locations_full["A"] = (seg:2, pos:0) ``` - both weight propagation purposes as well as the insertion purpose of full/empty block of arrival, the choice of introducing dual maps is much easier than differentiation at `unfinalized_block` level or using `chain_link` fields. - the key currently for both the map is `block_root`. A previous approach was made to keep unfinalized_locations_full maps key as `execution_hash` and unfinalized_locations_empty through `block_root`. But there was significant overhead in terms of number of conversion calla/reverse lookup for hash to root and viceversa. plus as only one variant of full/empty per blockroot can reach till forkchoice, there is ideally no problem with having the same keys. - a way to move forward with the changes is to look at in which scenarios(insertion into segment, calculation supporting vote, tiebraker , weight propagtion/childern filter/setting `ForkChoicePayloadStatus`) empty vs full is preferred across spec and current code.

title: Optimize computation of unrealized checkpoints
body:
# Fork choice: skip `process_justification_and_finalization` when result is provably unchanged

Implements the optimization described in the existing `TODO(Grandine Team)` comment in `fork_choice_store/src/store.rs`. Referenced lighthouse for the appropriate change.

When computing unrealized checkpoints for a new block in epoch N, if the parent's unrealized justified checkpoint is already at epoch N and its unrealized finalized checkpoint is at epoch N−1, no block in this epoch can push those checkpoints any higher. The child block inherits the parent's values directly and the O(validators) `process_justification_and_finalization` call is skipped. This fires roughly one third of the time under normal finality conditions.

cargo test --release --no-default-features --features default-networks,blst \
  --workspace \
  --exclude zkvm_host --exclude zkvm_guest_risc0 \

title: Log EL SYNCING status at debug instead of warn
body:
While the execution layer is syncing, `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` and `engine_newPayload` return SYNCING, which is a normal and expected status. Grandine continues optimistically and control flow is unchanged, so logging it at `warn` is just noise during EL sync (the subject of #217).

This downgrades both SYNCING branches in `execution_service.rs` from `warn_with_peers!` to `debug_with_peers!`. The INVALID and call-failure branches stay at `warn`. The detail is still available via `GRANDINE_LOG=eth1_api=debug` (the default filter is `eth1_api=info`).

Re #217.

**Scope note:** #217 also mentions a `request_with_fallback` warning in `eth1_api/http_api.rs` that fires on a JSON-RPC `-32001` "Receipt not available" error during EL sync. I left that path unchanged on purpose: it is a generic RPC-error handler that also marks the endpoint offline and increments error metrics, and there is no EL-sync-state signal at that layer — downgrading it via error-code/string matching would hide genuine endpoint failures. A proper fix would plumb EL-sync state into that layer; happy to follow up separately, so I've left #217 open.

(Saw @DarkLord017 expressed interest earlier, but the issue was unassigned with no follow-up — happy to coordinate, and the deferred `request_with_fallback` case is up for grabs.)

title: Process Electra and Single attestations in the slasher
body:
## Summary

The slasher was silently dropping `Attestation::Electra` and `Attestation::Single` from its detection path, so attester-slashing detection has been effectively dead on mainnet since the Electra fork.

This change unifies the slasher's internal `IndexedAttestation` and `AttesterSlashing` types on the Electra form (Electra's bound supersets Phase 0's, and the live network is post-Electra). The three attestation kinds are handled as follows:

- `Attestation::Single`: built directly from `attester_index` into an Electra `IndexedAttestation` via `ContiguousList::try_from_iter`.
- `Attestation::Electra`: passed through `electra::get_indexed_attestation`.
- `Attestation::Phase0`: widened to Electra via `ContiguousList::try_from_iter` (Phase 0's `MaxValidatorsPerCommittee` bound is a subset of Electra's `MaxAttestersPerSlot`).

`process_attester_slashing` now emits `CombinedAttesterSlashing::Electra`. The change ripples through `slasher/src/{attestations,indexed_attestations,messages,status,targets}.rs`, `validator/src/validator.rs`, and a 3-line comment in `block_producer/src/block_producer.rs` documenting the intentional pre-Electra filter drop.

## Tests

Three new tests:

- `single_attestation_converts_to_single_index_indexed_attestation` (slasher.rs): Single → Electra `IndexedAttestation` round-trip.
- `phase0_indexed_attestation_widens_preserving_indices_data_and_signature` (slasher.rs): Phase 0 → Electra widening preserves all fields.
- `detects_double_vote_for_each_attester_in_multi_index_attestation` (attestations.rs): multi-attester double-vote detection path.

`cargo test -p slasher`: 9/9 pass. `cargo check -p validator`: clean.

## Compat notes

- Fork choice and block production re-validate independently, so the always-Electra-output choice does not affect their correctness.
- `AttestationData` is fork-independent, so existing slasher DB entries remain byte-compatible.
- SSZ encoding of an Electra `IndexedAttestation` containing a single index has the same on-wire shape as a Phase 0 `IndexedAttestation` with the same index, modulo the `attesting_indices` type bound.

Fixes #655.

title: Store attestations with pristine data in the aggregate pool
body:
Part of #780. This is the "representation cleanup" step from [this comment](https://github.com/grandinetech/grandine/issues/780#issuecomment-5005509645).

### Problem

The aggregate pool stores attestations in phase0 form and reuses `AttestationData.index` as a scratch field for the committee index. All three ingestion paths write to it, and the outbound conversion hardcodes it back to `0`. This is lossless on Electra/Fulu (`index` is always zero there), but Gloas revives the field as the payload-availability vote (`assert data.index < 2`), covered by the attester's signature. With the current representation the vote is destroyed on ingestion, and two attestations that differ only in their payload vote collapse into the same pool bucket, merging signatures across different signing roots.

### Approach

Committee index is an organizational dimension of the pool, not signed data, so it moves into an explicit `PoolKey { data, committee_index }` map key, and `data` stays byte-for-byte as signed (Electra: `index == 0`, Gloas: payload vote preserved).

Scope is deliberately limited to storage. The packer, block-production, and HTTP-API boundaries still receive the old scratch representation via an explicitly temporary `rehydrate_phase0_scratch_repr` helper (marked `TODO(#780)`), so pre-Gloas behaviour is byte-identical and this PR changes no observable behaviour. The rehydration is removed in the next step (greedy baseline), when the packer consumes pristine data directly.

Two refinements from the plan comment. First, investigation showed network aggregates are single-committee per spec, so the pool keeps its single-committee width and the committee index moves into the key rather than storing full Electra containers. Second, the `electra::get_attesting_indices` switch moves to the greedy-baseline PR, where it belongs together with the packer consuming pristine data.

The two external read sites of the scratch `data.index` (`block_producer` and the aggregate-attestation HTTP handler) now go through the canonical committee accessor instead.

### Testing

The existing packing snapshot tests feed attestations directly into the packer and bypass pool conversion, storage, and emission, so they don't cover this path. Added round-trip unit tests (no eth2-cache needed):

- phase0 round-trip is byte-identical (structural and `hash_tree_root` equality)
- Electra ingestion keeps `data` pristine and extracts the committee index into the key
- Gloas payload votes 0/1 land in distinct pool keys and are never merged
- `SingleAttestation` conversion no longer overwrites `data.index`

Two of these are portable to the pre-fix code and fail there (`single_conversion_keeps_gloas_votes_distinct`, `single_conversion_keeps_data_index_pristine`), confirming they are genuine regression tests for the Gloas issue.

One deliberate edge-case change: the v2 aggregate-attestation lookup previously compared roots after resetting `index` to 0, producing a root that matches nothing for genuine phase0 data; it now matches against the pristine stored key. This only affects hypothetical pre-Electra queries through the v2 endpoint (Electra+ in practice) and is a strict improvement.

### Next

Greedy baseline: remove the solver path and the rehydration boundary, move on-chain aggregation into the packer so selection operates in block-budget units (8). Payload attestations (PTC) will be a separate issue.

title: block production: wire Gloas builder bid fetch and notify
body:
Part of #769
Depends on #819.

## Summary
Wires the Gloas Staked Builder API into block production:

- During propose, fetch an execution payload bid over HTTP in parallel with local payload prep, validate it through fork choice (`on_api_execution_payload_bid`), then select the highest-value bid among accepted HTTP and gossip bids (self-build if none).
- Optionally sign `RequestAuth` with local keys when a bid fetch will run.
- After gossiping the signed beacon block, notify the builder via `submitSignedBeaconBlock` for external builders (best-effort). Accepted HTTP bids are also re-gossiped so peers can see them before the block.

## Behavior
- Pre-Gloas path is unchanged (blinded header / `post_blinded_block`).
- On Gloas, gossip remains the primary bid source; HTTP fetch is an additional path for builders that expose the Staked Builder API.
- Ordering for external builder proposals: sign → `on_own_block` → gossip beacon block → HTTP notify.
- `submitSignedBeaconBlock` is notify-only (202); the proposer still gossips the block.
- Web3Signer does not support RequestAuth yet; those validators fetch without auth (logged at info).
- HTTP preferences (`submitBuilderPreferences`) and skipping `register_validators` at Gloas are follow-ups.

## Test plan
- `cargo test -p builder_api --features blst`
- `cargo test -p signer -p kzg_utils --features bls/blst,kzg_utils/blst request_auth`
- On a Gloas setup with `--builder-api-url`: confirm HTTP 200 bids are selected and the builder is notified after gossip; 204 and invalid bids fall back to gossip/self-build; self-build skips HTTP fetch and notify; the block is gossiped regardless of notify result.

title: Remove the solver-based attestation packing path
body:
Part of #780. Stacked on #820 (merge that first); this is the first half of the "greedy baseline" step from the plan comment.

### Why

The solver path (`pack_proposable_attestations_optimally`) decomposes the packing problem per attestation-data group and allocates the block budget across groups with a knapsack DP over `MaxAttestations = 128`, counted in per-committee attestations. Post-Electra, blocks are limited to `MAX_ATTESTATIONS_ELECTRA = 8` merged on-chain aggregates, so the DP allocates along an axis that no longer corresponds to anything the block can hold — the optimization target itself is stale. Rather than reworking the ILP formulation around the new unit, this removes the path entirely so the follow-up PR can rebuild packing around the real budget. (Measurement on cached Goerli data backs this up: a plain best-per-committee greedy already covers 99.89% of observed attesters, so a solver has near-zero headroom to buy.)

### What

- `pack_proposable_attestations_optimally` and its solver-only helpers (`find_optimal_selections`, the ILP max-cover selection, per-validator weight tables, and associated constants) are deleted: −783 lines.
- The `good_lp`/HiGHS dependency is dropped from the workspace, removing the solver from the supply-chain surface.
- The background pre-pack task previously ran an optimal→greedy anytime loop; it now runs a single greedy pass. The serving architecture (pre-pack then serve) is unchanged.
- One behaviour-relevant function turned out to be misnamed rather than solver-specific: the "should pack optimally" gate actually guarded pre-packing on unsupported forks (Fulu). It is kept and renamed to `is_pre_pack_supported`, so fork gating is preserved bit-for-bit.

### Testing

Greedy is untouched, and the existing packing snapshot tests (which exercise only the greedy path) pass unchanged. `cargo check` is clean across the workspace with the solver dependency removed.

title: feat(checkpoint-sync): support syncing from trusted non-finalized checkpoints
body:
## Summary

This is an implementation-first, iterative PR exploring how Grandine can safely bootstrap and sync from an operator-selected trusted non-finalized checkpoint.

Grandine currently assumes that its checkpoint-sync startup anchor is finalized. Supporting a non-finalized starting point affects checkpoint loading, fork-choice initialization, storage, forward-sync boundaries, P2P status, Beacon API semantics, and restart behavior.

Following feedback from the Grandine team, this PR does not treat the original design proposal as a fixed architecture. I will continue implementing and testing the feature here, document the assumptions exposed by the existing code, and shape the final design from those findings.

The implementation will remain based on the latest Glamsterdam branch while this work is in progress.

## Goal

Enable Grandine to start and sync forward from an explicitly trusted non-finalized checkpoint without treating or advertising that checkpoint as protocol-finalized.

The completed implementation should:

- preserve the existing finalized checkpoint-sync behavior;
- load and validate an explicitly selected checkpoint block and state;
- use the selected checkpoint as a trusted local startup boundary;
- preserve the real on-chain justified and finalized checkpoints;
- report correct finality through P2P and the Beacon API;
- use safe forward-sync boundaries;
- clearly document its trust assumptions and limitations.

## Implementation approach

This work follows an implementation-first approach:

1. Make the smallest change needed to load a selected checkpoint.
2. Pass it through Grandine’s existing startup path.
3. Test the behavior on a live network.
4. Record where the implementation assumes that the anchor is finalized.
5. Introduce only the abstractions required by the observed behavior.
6. Repeat testing after each change.
7. Keep the PR rebased on the latest Glamsterdam branch.

The final proposed design will be based on the implementation findings and Grandine team feedback.

## Current implementation

The first iteration adds:

```bash
--checkpoint-sync-block-id <BLOCK_ID>
```

Supported Beacon API block identifiers include:

- `finalized`;
- `head`;
- a slot;
- a block root.

When the option is omitted, Grandine continues selecting `finalized`, preserving the existing checkpoint-sync behavior.

Example experimental usage:

```bash
grandine \
  --network hoodi \
  --checkpoint-sync-url https://example-beacon-node \
  --checkpoint-sync-block-id head \
  --force-checkpoint-sync
```

An explicit non-finalized selection trusts the configured remote Beacon API.

### Remote loading

The existing finalized-only remote loader has been generalized to accept a `BlockId`.

The loading flow currently:

1. Fetches the selected remote block.
2. Normalizes it to an epoch-start anchor when required by the current startup path.
3. Fetches the state at the selected anchor slot.
4. Validates the downloaded block and state.
5. Passes the pair through the existing storage and startup path.

### Block and state validation

Before startup continues, the implementation checks:

```rust
block.message().state_root() == state.hash_tree_root()
```

and:

```rust
accessors::latest_block_root(&state)
    == block.message().hash_tree_root()
```

This prevents inconsistent remote block/state responses from reaching the assertions in `Store::new`.

### Existing finalized behavior

A predefined remotely loaded checkpoint is reused only when the selected identifier is:

```rust
BlockId::Finalized
```

Explicit selections such as `head`, a slot, or a block root are loaded from the configured remote Beacon API.

## Manual testing

I tested the first iteration on Hoodi using:

- Grandine as the consensus client;
- Reth as the execution client;
- a public Hoodi Beacon API as the checkpoint source;
- a fresh Grandine data directory.

I first verified that the existing finalized checkpoint-sync path continued to work.

I then tested:

```text
--checkpoint-sync-block-id head
```

The experimental path successfully completed:

```text
head selection
    ↓
remote block loading
    ↓
epoch-start normalization
    ↓
matching state loading
    ↓
block/state validation
    ↓
storage initialization
    ↓
P2P startup
    ↓
Beacon API startup
    ↓
forward block processing
```

Grandine initialized successfully, connected to Reth, started its networking and HTTP services, and processed blocks forward from the initial anchor.

## Findings from the first iteration

The loading and startup experiment succeeded, but it exposed an important distinction between BeaconState finality and Grandine’s fork-choice store finality.

### BeaconState finality

The downloaded `BeaconState` retained the network’s real:

- previous justified checkpoint;
- current justified checkpoint;
- finalized checkpoint.

This confirms that downloading a non-finalized block and its state does not itself lose the protocol checkpoint information.

### Fork-choice initialization

`Store::new` currently creates a checkpoint from the startup anchor:

```rust
let checkpoint = Checkpoint {
    epoch,
    root: block_root,
};
```

It then uses that checkpoint for:

```text
current_justified_checkpoint
finalized_checkpoint
unrealized_justified_checkpoint
unrealized_finalized_checkpoint
```

The store-level justified and finalized checkpoints are also initialized from the same anchor.

This means the downloaded state can preserve the correct protocol checkpoints while the fork-choice store still treats the trusted startup anchor as finalized.

### Beacon API behavior

The finalized-header API resolves through:

```text
BlockId::Finalized
    → controller.last_finalized_block()
    → store.last_finalized()
```

During testing, `/headers/finalized` returned the local head instead of the block represented by the downloaded state’s actual finalized checkpoint.

This is a concrete result of initializing store finality from the trusted startup anchor.

### P2P implications

Grandine constructs its local P2P status using:

```text
controller.finalized_epoch()
controller.finalized_root()
```

These values also originate from the fork-choice store.

Until startup trust and protocol finality are separated, the experimental path may advertise the trusted startup point—or later incorrectly finalized blocks—as protocol-finalized to peers.

### Sync implications

Forward sync currently derives its lower boundary from:

```text
snapshot.finalized_epoch()
```

The initial anchor is also written under finalized storage structures such as:

```text
FinalizedBlockByRoot
```

This means the required separation affects more than the finalized Beacon API response. It also affects P2P status, storage, sync boundaries, and potentially restart behavior.

## Current design direction

The implementation findings suggest that Grandine needs to distinguish between:

```text
trusted local startup boundary
```

and:

```text
protocol justified and finalized checkpoints
```

However, this PR intentionally does not commit to a large anchor abstraction or architectural rewrite yet.

The next iterations will determine the smallest safe representation and the minimum set of components that need to change.

## Planned iterations

### Iteration 1: Selected checkpoint loading

- Add an optional checkpoint block selector.
- Preserve `finalized` as the default.
- Load the selected remote block.
- Retain epoch-start normalization.
- Load the corresponding state.
- Validate block/state consistency.
- Pass the checkpoint through the existing startup path.
- Test startup and forward processing on Hoodi.

### Iteration 2: Startup trust and fork choice

- Preserve the state’s actual justified checkpoint during initialization.
- Preserve the state’s actual finalized checkpoint during initialization.
- Represent the trusted startup boundary separately where required.
- Prevent fork choice from rolling back below the trusted boundary.
- Avoid treating unavailable pre-anchor history as locally finalized.
- Add focused fork-choice initialization tests.

### Iteration 3: Protocol-facing behavior

- Ensure `/headers/finalized` resolves actual protocol finality.
- Ensure finalized state and block identifiers retain their protocol meaning.
- Ensure P2P status advertises the real finalized root and epoch.
- Verify peer grouping and status validation behavior.
- Review forward-sync lower-bound handling.

### Iteration 4: Storage and restart

- Determine whether the trusted boundary needs separate persistence.
- Avoid persisting a non-finalized anchor as finalized history.
- Test restart behavior.
- Review back-sync behavior and initial limitations.

### Additional testing

- Test explicit slot selection.
- Test explicit block-root selection.
- Test unavailable blocks and states.
- Test block/state mismatch rejection.
- Test finalized checkpoint-sync regressions.
- Test P2P status after non-finalized startup.
- Test forward sync after non-finalized startup.
- Test restart and persistence behavior.

## Current limitations

This remains an experimental implementation.

The non-finalized path is not currently safe for production because:

- the trusted startup anchor is still used as fork-choice finality;
- P2P status may report incorrect finality;
- finalized Beacon API identifiers may resolve incorrectly;
- initial storage treats the anchor as finalized;
- forward-sync boundaries still depend on store finality;
- restart and persistence behavior have not been addressed.

The existing finalized checkpoint-sync path remains the supported default.

## Verification

The current iteration has been checked with:

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

```bash
cargo check \
  -p grandine \
  --features default-networks
```

```bash
cargo test \
  -p runtime \
  --features default-networks,bls/blst,kzg_utils/blst \
  checkpoint_sync_
```

The focused checkpoint-selector tests pass.

## Review focus

As this PR evolves, I would especially appreciate feedback on:

1. Whether `BlockId` is the appropriate operator-facing selector.
2. Whether the initial implementation should remain restricted to epoch-start anchors.
3. Whether the remote block/state validation belongs in the checkpoint loader.
4. Which component should own the trusted startup boundary.
5. How to initialize fork choice with the state’s real justified and finalized checkpoints when their blocks precede the locally available anchor.
6. Which storage and sync paths must distinguish local availability from protocol finality.
7. What the least invasive safe implementation would look like.

## Status

The first loading and startup iteration works, but complete non-finalized checkpoint sync is not implemented yet.

This PR will continue evolving based on implementation findings and Grandine team feedback. The final design will be presented for deeper review once the required behavior and component boundaries are clearer.

title: Validate bid gas limit against the payload at bid.parent_block_hash
body:
## What

`Store::validate_execution_payload_bid` derived `parent_gas_limit` from `state_at(bid.parent_block_root).latest_execution_payload_bid().gas_limit` — the parent block's own bid — regardless of which payload the bid builds on. The spec keys the check on the payload the bid actually extends:

```python
parent_gas_limit = seen.execution_payloads[bid.parent_block_hash].gas_limit
```
(https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/a670e0193446474bb1775ec94a93ca6fbaa11a89/specs/gloas/p2p-interface.md#L995-L1000)

A bid with `parent_block_root = head` and `parent_block_hash = head_bid.parent_block_hash` (head payload treated as withheld — which `is_bid_compatible_with_head` permits when `should_build_on_full` is false) must be checked against the grandparent payload's gas limit. Whenever the gas limit is moving, that differs from the head bid's gas limit by one EIP-1559 step, so a spec-correct bid was dropped with `bid gas_limit is not compatible with target_gas_limit` — on gossip, and via `POST /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_bids`, where it results in a 200 with an `Ignore` and no broadcast.

This PR resolves the chain link carrying the payload identified by `bid.parent_block_hash` through the existing `execution_payload_locations` index (replacing the bare `contains_key` existence check) and uses the gas limit committed by that block: its bid post-Gloas, the execution payload itself for a pre-Gloas block at the fork boundary. Envelopes must match their bid's `gas_limit` (already enforced at envelope processing), so the bid value is the payload value. `ExecutionPayload::gas_limit` is added to the trait for the pre-Gloas case.

## Why

Seen on glamsterdam-devnet-8 (gas limit ramping under EIP-8261). Slot 85165: payload at 85163 had gas limit 199411976, payload at 85164 (head) had 199606713, target 200000000. A builder's parent-empty bid carried 199606713 = 199411976 + 199411976/1024 − 1, correct for the payload it builds on; comparing against the head bid (199606713) makes it look like it failed to step toward the target.

Same class of bug was found in prysm (https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17405), lighthouse (https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/pull/9905) and nimbus (https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/pull/8941); lodestar and teku are correct. The spec gossip test vectors don't cover empty-head bids yet (every case uses the head's own payload as `parent_block_hash`); a vector PR is in progress.

## Testing

`cargo check` / `cargo clippy -p grandine --no-default-features --features default-networks,bls/blst,kzg_utils/blst` and `cargo fmt --check` on the changed crates. Targeting `glamsterdam-devnet-8` per the devnet image; happy to retarget or forward-port.

title: Key attestation packer candidates by committee, not AttestationData alone
body:
## What

`AttestationPacker::pack_proposable_attestations_greedily` de-duplicates candidate aggregates keyed on `AttestationData` alone — in the `into_grouping_map_by(|(aggregate, _)| aggregate.data)` pass and in the `candidates` `BTreeMap`. Post-Electra `data.index` no longer identifies the committee (and in Gloas it carries the payload-presence vote), so every committee's aggregate for a slot shares the same `AttestationData`, and the grouping keeps only the single highest-weight committee. The block producer then receives one committee per slot and packs a single-committee on-chain aggregate.

This PR keys both collections by `PoolAttestation::key()` (`AttestationKey { data, committee_index }`) instead. `attesting_indices`, `added_weight` and `add_attestation` already operate per committee via `committee_index`, and the block producer already merges same-`data` attestations across committees with `compute_on_chain_aggregate`, so nothing else needs to change.

## Why

The keying dates from 2024 and was masked until recently: pre-Electra `data.index` *is* the committee index, and after 63806e0e ("Store attestations with pristine data in the aggregate pool") the pool still emitted a scratch representation with `data.index = committee_index` for the packer. f83d952c ("Attestation pool refactor for epbs") removed that shim and moved the packer onto `PoolAttestation`, but left the `data`-keyed collapse in place. The packer's own tests didn't catch it because they use pre-Electra Goerli/Holesky fixtures and build `PoolAttestation { committee_index: data.index, .. }`, where `data` is unique per committee.

Observed on glamsterdam-devnet-8 (image at 8700067d): every Grandine-proposed block contains exactly one attestation covering one committee (~132 of ~2636 votes for the slot), while every other CL packs the full 20-committee aggregate. Over 4 epochs, 95% of previous-slot votes are left out whenever Grandine proposes the next block, versus ~0% for the other clients; network-wide that's ~16% of all attestations landing at inclusion distance 2 and an average inclusion distance of 1.21 on every client's dashboard row. Grandine's own `attestation packer candidates count` log line shows 4–7 candidates per block on a 20-committee network — the number of distinct `AttestationData` values.

Example (slot / proposer / attestations as `{inclusion delay: (count, committees, bits)}`):

```
92246  lodestar-ethrex-1    atts=1  {-1: (1, 20, 2634)}
92247  grandine-nimbusel-2  atts=1  {-1: (1,  1,  132)}
92248  grandine-nimbusel-1  atts=2  {-2: (1,  1,  132), -1: (1, 1, 132)}
92249  nimbus-reth-2        atts=3  {-3: (1, 18, 2371), -2: (1, 19, 2504), -1: (1, 20, 2635)}
```

This affects any post-Electra network running this branch, not only Gloas.

## Testing

`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo check -p grandine --no-default-features --features default-networks,bls/blst,kzg_utils/blst`. (`cargo clippy` currently fails on this branch before reaching `operation_pools` with a pre-existing `lint_groups_priority` error in the workspace `Cargo.toml` lints table — unrelated to this change.) No new unit test: the packer tests are gated on `eth2-cache` fixtures that are all pre-Electra, so a regression test needs an Electra/Gloas fixture — happy to add one if you can point me at the preferred way to build such a state in tests. Targeting `glamsterdam-devnet-8` per the devnet image; happy to retarget or forward-port.

title: Delta database implementation
body:
Implemented delta-encoding for states. 

The state delta-encoding has several advantages:
  1. Reduced space requirements. Previously, archival mode persisted one state every 32 epochs. For mainnet, this meant states occupied 1.5-2Tb in archival node. Delta-encoded states take only fraction of it - around 150-200Gb instead.
  2. Improve state loading performance. Old version tried to load closest to requested state snapshot, then apply all subsequent blocks on it. This meant that we had to load ~200MB ssz+snappy compressed state snapshot into memory, deserialize it, then apply 0-1024 state transitions for it. This also means that state is "cold" - its caches are empty. Now, we usually take state that is already in memory (via caching), meaning we skip snapshot deserialization step, loading only tiny (comparing to state snapshot) delta from disk (around 150Kb-1.5Mb), apply 0-32 state transitions for it, and the state itself is "warm", making hashing much faster.
  3. Reduced memory usage. Old version deserialized and instantiated completely new state in-memory, for every request through API. The state-at-slot cache made this situation even worse, because it kept this state in memory for large amounts of time. The developed patching algorithm applies deltas on existing states, allowing to reuse memory through structural sharing, as well as caches.

Several bugs and improvements made along the way:
  1. The `load_state_by_iteration` function accidentally loaded all blocks from the database, before deciding which ones to choose. Added early termination condition, for stopping when we've found necessary block.
  2. Capped archival persisting tasks. Previously, archiving tasks were unbounded, meaning, they were spawned as many times, as forkchoice mutator decided to offload states. New archiving tasks consume more memory than old ones (because they write more information to database), so unbounded archival tasks just crashed node sometimes. Replaced this with archival threadpool, that scales with incoming task count, queues persistance tasks if all threads are occupied, and blocks on current thread if queue is full.
  3. Added possibility to write raw values to database. This allows to use zstd compression when needed, as well as more complicated compression schemes (like deltas use, where fields are compressed separately).
  4. Implemented SSZ serialization for Option<T> type, so that deltas can avoid wasting memory, and not saving values if they weren't changed.

This database change is backwards compatible, and users do not need to resync their nodes. Full nodes will free storage automatically (newly arrived states will be written using delta-encoding, while old ones eventually will be pruned). Archival nodes need to resync from scratch, otherwise old states won't be converted to delta format, thus taking up space. 

Closes both #716 and #717.

title: Fix pubkey recovery for unfinalized states
body:
When unfinalized states are persisted, their keys are zeroized in the same way as keys in finalized states. However, restoring public keys for unfinalized states requires more care: only zeroized keys should be restored, rather than replacing all keys.

This fixes two bugs:

  - unfinalized states with more validators than the latest finalized state failed to load because pubkey recovery crashed when the finalized state's key list was too short;
  - unfinalized states with the same number of public keys as the finalized state could be loaded incorrectly when keys at the end of the list differed, because those keys were blindly replaced.

title: Replace EF bootnodes with NodeOps fleet
body:
I am on the Ethereum Foundation's Node Infrastructure team (NodeOps). We run the bootnodes
that ship in this repository as the "EF" entries for mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi. We are
replacing that fleet, and we would like the new records in a release before the Glamsterdam
client releases.

### What changes

- Add five new EF bootnodes per network. Every node serves all three networks.
- Remove the legacy EF entries. The new set is a replacement, not an addition.
- Third-party bootnodes and DNS discovery roots are untouched.

### The new fleet

Five bootnodes, each serving mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi. They are geographically distributed,
multi-cloud, and dual stack (IPv4 + IPv6). Each node runs discv4 and discv5 on the EL port and
discv5 on the CL port, and the fleet spreads across several discovery implementations so one
implementation bug cannot take the whole set down.

### About the records

- The ENRs are generic bootnode records: no `eth2` field, no `tcp`, sequence number 1. Clients
  dial configured bootnodes regardless of fork, and a static list cannot be re-signed every
  fork, so we do not include fork data on purpose.
- Where an EL list accepts ENRs, we list the ENR. It covers discv4 and discv5 and carries the
  IPv6 endpoint. Enodes appear only where a list needs them, in the discovery-only form
  `enode://<pubkey>@<ip>:0?discport=<port>` (no RLPx listener).
- The records are derived from the node keys and are byte-identical across all the client
  PRs. The canonical copies are the eth-clients PRs (`metadata/bootstrap_nodes.yaml` and
  `metadata/enodes.yaml` for mainnet, sepolia and hoodi).

### Verification

- Each node answers discv4 and discv5 pings from the public internet on the advertised ports.
- The relevant tests in this repository pass with the new lists (details below).
- The legacy nodes stay online until client releases with the new records are widely deployed.
  We will announce the shutdown separately.

### Contact

Chase Wright, EF Node Infrastructure. Discord `MysticRyuujin` (ETH R&D and STEEL servers), or
chase.wright@ethereum.org.

### This repository

**Files:** `runtime/src/predefined_network.rs`.

**Semantics:** `MAINNET_BOOTNODES`, `SEPOLIA_BOOTNODES` and `HOODI_BOOTNODES` swap the EF ENRs
(4 / 5 / 6) for the five new CL ENRs. Entries mirror the eth-clients PRs.

title: Run the validator client against remote beacon nodes with the new vc and bn commands
body:
`grandine vc --beacon-node-urls ...` runs the validator client alone against remote beacon nodes, `grandine bn` runs the beacon node alone, and the bare command runs the beacon node with the local validator when one is configured. Duties come from exactly one source: the built-in node or the remote nodes. vc refuses options that only the built-in beacon node acts on.

The validator no longer holds the fork choice controller. It works through a ChainSource, and every duty goes through the BeaconNodeApi trait, which the built-in node and the remote nodes both implement: attester, aggregation, sync committee, PTC, proposer, payload attestation, voluntary exit and doppelganger liveness duties, plus prepared proposers, validator registrations and proposer preferences. Attestation data returned by a remote node is validated for the reported index and target epoch before it is signed. Proposer preferences are published for the dependent root the duties are held under.

Remote nodes are polled for health and ranked by it, then by the newest head; an unreachable node is kept as the last choice. Requests have per-endpoint timeouts, a head stream tracks reorgs, and a slot head fallback covers a node that falls behind. Duties are published to every node by default, returning once one accepts; the payload envelope goes to the node that produced the block. In remote mode the validator is driven by clock ticks directly, and genesis is agreed with the nodes before it starts.

Resolves own validator indices from the finalized state, driven by events.

Register the validator client with the beacon nodes' builder via --use-builder pre-gloas, skipping validators without a fee recipient

Stop counting sync committee messages as validator liveness

Run the doppelganger check late in the slot
At the aggregate tick every node has ticked into the epoch and seen the slot's attestations

Leave the peer counts out of validator client logs

Identify the chain by its genesis validators root without loading the state; vc and the interchange commands use the predefined network's root, read from the embedded mainnet state or a constant for the testnets;

Run data column recovery on the reconstruction executor

Accept a slot's worth of aggregates in one publish request

Doppelganger protection no longer reads the local beacon state or the liveness tracker directly: it takes validator indices and a liveness query from the caller, so it works against remote beacon nodes, where only synced nodes are asked and a validator seen live by any of them counts as live. A key is activated only after a successful check, a failed query postpones activation instead of panicking, and a key whose index is unknown is not activated until its index resolves and a full check window has passed from that point.

title: Count BPO forks in ENR next_fork_epoch
body:
The ENR `eth2` field ignores a BPO fork that is scheduled before the next regular fork.

The [Fulu p2p spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/82b6e507dc31f6f7052e79b16ecfe3778c1b38f6/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#eth2-field) says that `next_fork_epoch` is the epoch of the next fork, "whether a regular fork _or a BPO fork_". It also says that `next_fork_version` "will only change for regular forks, _not BPO forks_". `enr_fork_id` uses `next_phase_at_slot` first, and that function counts only regular forks. Example: the current fork is Fulu, with a BPO fork at epoch A and Gloas at epoch B > A. Grandine advertises (Gloas, B). The spec requires (Fulu, A).

This PR moves the calculation into `compute_enr_fork_id` and derives it from `chain_config` and the slot:

- `next_fork_epoch` is the earlier of the next regular fork and the next `blob_schedule` entry. A blob entry counts only at or after `fulu_fork_epoch`, as in `compute_fork_digest`. An entry at `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH` does not count.
- `next_fork_version` is the next regular fork's version if that fork is at `next_fork_epoch`. Otherwise it is the current version, because a BPO fork does not change the version. If nothing is scheduled, it is the current version with `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH`.

The `enr_fork_id_next_fork` table covers these cases: a BPO before, at, and after a regular fork, a BPO only, nothing scheduled, pre-Fulu, a BPO at the Fulu epoch, a blob entry before Fulu, a blob entry at `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH`, a past BPO, and Gloas scheduled without Fulu. Each row also checks `fork_digest`.

Prysm, Lodestar, and Nimbus already use this rule. Spec issue: ethereum/consensus-specs#5701

To run the tests locally, I added `kzg_utils = { workspace = true, features = ["blst"] }` to the `p2p` dev-dependencies, because a `p2p`-only build does not select a KZG backend. The `grandine` binary selects one by default. That line is not in this PR.

```
cargo test -p p2p --features bls/blst
```

title: Implement Gloas builder flow from beacon-APIs
body:
**Specs:** [beacon-APIs#630](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/630), [keymanager-APIs#88](https://github.com/ethereum/keymanager-APIs/pull/88) (with [#93](https://github.com/ethereum/keymanager-APIs/pull/93), [#94](https://github.com/ethereum/keymanager-APIs/pull/94)), [builder-specs#138](https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/138) (with [#165](https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/165), [#168](https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/168))

 #### Beacon API
 - `POST /eth/v4/validator/blocks/{slot}` takes a `BuilderConfig` body, requests a bid from each builder entry while the block body is built, and picks the winner by `builder_boost_factor * (value + min(execution_payment, max_execution_payment))` against the local payload. It validates those bids against the block production state before selection. Returns `Eth-Builder-Url` when a builder API bid wins.
 - `POST /eth/v2/beacon/blocks` forwards the signed block to the `Eth-Builder-Url` builder after publishing.
 - `POST /eth/v1/validator/builder_preferences` submits each entry to its builder.
 
 #### Keymanager API
 - `GET`/`POST`/`DELETE /eth/v1/validator/{pubkey}/builder_config`. `GET` returns the fully resolved config, `POST` replaces it, `DELETE` resets it. Invalid configs (missing `url`, duplicate `url` + `auth_data`, a nonzero `max_execution_payment` without the opt-in) are rejected.
  - Per-key configs are validated when `validators.yml` loads.
  
 #### Built-in validator
- In the epoch before each proposal, it submits builder preferences to the key's builders and caches the signed auths to reuse during bid requests from builder APIs.
- When proposing, it requests bids from the key's builders alongside the local payload, and forwards the beacon block to the builder whose bid won.

#### Builder API client
- Implements client requests to builder API endpoints: `getExecutionPayloadBid`, `submitBuilderPreferences` and `submitSignedBeaconBlock`.
- Request bodies follow `--builder-api-format`. A builder that answers an SSZ body with 415 or 406 gets the request again in JSON, and JSON from then on.

#### Testing
Kurtosis devnet with buildoor `builder_api` enabled connected to a grandine node with Lodestar VC (beacon api path) and a grandine node with its built-in validator.

  - el_type: geth

    vc_type: lodestar
    vc_image: chainsafe/lodestar:latest
    vc_extra_params:
      - "--builder.urls=http://buildoor-grandine-geth-1:8080,http://builder-a.invalid:18550"
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethpandaops/geth:master
    cl_type: lighthouse
    cl_image: ethpandaops/lighthouse:unstable
    cl_log_level: debug
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethpandaops/geth:master
    cl_type: grandine
    cl_binary_path: "./binaries/grandine-minimal"
    cl_force_restart: true
    cl_extra_env_vars:
      GRANDINE_LOG: "validator=debug,block_producer=debug,builder_api=debug,fork_choice_control=debug"
    cl_extra_params:

title: Add CodSpeed continuous performance benchmarks
body:
This PR sets up [CodSpeed](https://codspeed.io) to run the existing Criterion benchmarks in `benches/` on every push to `develop` and on every pull request. CodSpeed uses CPU simulation, so results stay consistent between runs, and it reports regressions directly on PRs.

## Changes

- **`Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock`**: the workspace `criterion` dependency now points at `codspeed-criterion-compat` (renamed to `criterion`). Benchmark code still imports `criterion::...`. Plain `cargo bench` behaves as before, because the compat crate forwards to Criterion when it is not built through `cargo codspeed`.
- **`benches/benches/*.rs`**: CodSpeed can only instrument benchmarks registered with `criterion_group!` / `criterion_main!`, so each hand-written `fn main()` is now a `run_benchmarks(criterion: &mut Criterion)` function registered through those macros. `criterion_main!` already calls `configure_from_args()` and `final_summary()`, so the explicit calls were removed. Other adjustments:
  - `transition_functions` and `fork_choice_control` now call `initialize_rayon().expect(...)` instead of using `?`, because benchmark functions return `()`.
  - `lookup_in_collection` now targets `BenchmarkGroup<'_, WallTime>` / `Bencher<'_>` instead of a generic `M: Measurement`, which the instrumented `Bencher` doesn't support.
  - In `fork_choice_control`, the `#[expect(clippy::too_many_lines)]` became unfulfilled after the change, so it was removed.
- **`.github/workflows/codspeed.yml`**: a new workflow that installs the same system packages as `ci.yml`, checks out the `dedicated_executor` and `eth2_libp2p` submodules, builds with `cargo codspeed build` (with the `blst` backend for `bls` and `kzg_utils`), and runs the benchmarks with `CodSpeedHQ/action@v5` in `simulation` mode. It authenticates with OIDC, so no token secret is needed.
- **`README.md`**: adds the CodSpeed badge.

## Benchmarks tracked in CI

These five suites don't need external data (232 benchmarks in total):

- `hashing`: `hashing::hash_*` compared with `sha2` and OpenSSL
- `shuffling`: `shuffle_slice` from 2^16 up to 2^20 validators
- `genesis`: a quick-start beacon state built from 1024 deposits
- `integer_square_root`: `integer_sqrt` compared with `num_integer`
- `lookup_in_collection`: lookups in `Vec`, `VecDeque`, `im::Vector`, `BTreeMap`, `OrdMap`, and hash maps

The other suites (`transition_functions`, `fork_choice_control`, `fork_choice_store`, `helper_functions`, `operation_pools`, `types`) were converted and compile, but CI doesn't run them. They load beacon states and blocks from the `eth2-cache` data set through `eth2_cache_utils`, and that data isn't available in this repository's submodules. If you can make that data available in CI (and the states are small enough for simulation), you can add them to the `--bench` lists in the workflow.

I ran the setup locally with `codspeed run -m simulation` and all five suites completed. The full run takes about 7–8 minutes, mostly in `genesis` and `shuffling`.

## Next steps

1. Merge this PR so `develop` gets a baseline. After that, PRs will get performance reports comparing against it.
2. Optionally, trigger the workflow manually (`workflow_dispatch`) to backfill historical data.
3. Consider adding the remaining suites once the `eth2-cache` data is available in CI.

Comment `@codspeedbot <request>` if you'd like changes, for example to add a benchmark for a specific function.

Fix clock deadlines at the Gloas fork boundary

When the next-tick search crosses into Gloas, it applies the new 750 ms tick
duration to the final pre-Gloas interval, which should still take one second.

## Description

Electra gossip requires `[REJECT]` when `attester_index` is not in the claimed committee. `Attestation::Single` converted to an indexed attestation without that check, and verifier prevalidation skips indexed validation, so a validly signed cross-committee attestation was Accepted.

Fixes #925

title: fork_choice_store: enforce committee membership for Attestation::Single gossip attestations
body:
Fixes #925, continuing from my Sep 29 trace in the issue thread.

## Root cause

A gossip `Attestation::Single` carries a claimed `attester_index`, and its conversion into an `IndexedAttestation` trusts that claim blindly: the index goes straight into `attesting_indices`, and the only follow-up check is the signature — over the pubkey of *whatever index was claimed*. Nothing enforces the spec's `[REJECT]` condition **"The attester is a member of the committee"**, so an attester can float an attestation from a validator outside the committee it names and have it propagated and counted toward fork choice.

## Fix

In `Store::attesting_indices` (`Attestation::Single` branch):

- resolve the beacon committee for the attestation's slot and committee index from the target state (same pattern as the aggregator check in `validate_aggregate_and_proof`)
- reject with the existing `AttestationConversionError::AttesterNotInCommittee` when the claimed attester is absent — it surfaces through the normal `AttestationValidationError::Other` wrap and the existing `P2pMessage::Reject` path

The check runs **unconditionally** — independent of `validate_indexed` — so the `skip_signatures=true` batch-prevalidation path rejects before the batch verifier ever sees the attestation. The stateless `TryFrom<SingleAttestation>` is left unchanged: membership needs the target state, which the store (and only the store) has at validation time.

Also makes `Context::controller()` `pub(crate)` so the regression test can drive `validate_attestation` directly.

## Verification

- New regression test `extra_tests::single_attestation_with_attester_outside_committee_is_rejected` (attester index `u64::MAX` against a committee of the minimal preset): **passes** — asserts the rejection carries `not in committee`
- `cargo check --workspace` (ci feature set, zkcrypto backend): clean with the patch
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean; `scripts/ci/clippy.bash`: exit 0

title: Fix inverted set difference in custody group backfill on startup
body:
## What is wrong

On startup, when the `custody_group_count` persisted in node metadata is lower
than the configured count, `Network::new` computes the columns to backfill as
`prev_sampling_columns.difference(&current_sampling_columns)`
(`p2p/src/network.rs`, in the `prev_custody_group_count < custody_group_count`
branch).

`get_custody_groups` iterates custody ids deterministically starting from
`node_id`, so the column set for a lower custody group count is a strict subset
of the set for a higher count. `prev \ current` is therefore always empty and
`RequestCustodyGroupBackfill` is never sent on this path. Introduced by #433.

## Effect

After a restart with an increased custody group count, the node advertises the
raised `custody_group_count` but never backfills the newly custodied columns,
so custody groups get backfilled wrong or not at all. The runtime path
(`update_data_column_subnets`, driven by validator custody requirement updates)
already uses the correct direction, which is why the bug only shows on restart.

## Fix

Compute `current_sampling_columns.difference(&prev_sampling_columns)` instead,
matching the existing runtime site. The difference is extracted into
`Network::backfill_column_indices` so its direction is covered by a unit test.

## Test

Added `network::tests::backfill_column_indices_returns_columns_added_by_custody_increase`.
It fails before the fix (`assertion failed: !backfill_column_indices.is_empty()`)
and passes after. It also asserts that a custody count decrease produces an
empty backfill set.

Follow-up to #377 and #433.

title: Implement aggregate-level greedy attestation packing for Gloas
body:
## TL;DR

Make Gloas attestation packing select final on-chain aggregates within the block limit. This is the greedy baseline for #780.

## Why

The existing path selects per-committee attestations before merging and truncating the result to eight on-chain aggregates. Selection therefore happens before the final block limit is applied.

## Changes

- Move on-chain aggregate construction into the packer, grouping by full attestation data to preserve Gloas payload votes.
- Select aggregates by marginal participation value and update scores after each selection.
- Count only successfully constructed aggregates toward the block limit. Failed construction consumes neither capacity nor participation.
- Recompute packing after the final bid, scoring against a state copy that reflects parent-payload processing. Process the completed block from the original state.

## Validation

Targeted release tests passed: 4 producer tests and 13 pool tests. Coverage includes aggregate selection and construction, self-build EMPTY and external-builder FULL proposals, and the Fulu-to-Gloas transition.

Manual synthetic benchmarks are included for packing-quality and runtime comparisons; they do not establish production latency.

## Notes

Packing still has no enforced deadline. Further optimization remains tracked in #780.

body:
`grandine vc` caches PTC and proposer duties under the dependent root the beacon node reports, and the fetched duties serve the slot that asked for them. The check rejecting a root that differs from the attester root is gone; beacon nodes disagree on the root for the Gloas fork epoch, so a separate validator client used to miss those duties.

Own PTC members are built one way whether duties come from a remote node or the built-in one: computed from the state or fetched for the requested indices, then filtered to held keys, deduplicated and sorted.

Own proposer duties are one entry per epoch, holding the reported root and the own proposals, in place of a map by root and slot plus a set of fetched epochs. A refetch replaces the epoch, so proposer preferences are signed under that root without comparing it to the attester root, and the duty path answers from a single read.

Also:
- Keep repeated attester and sync committee duties from a remote node once
- Restore the donation address fallback in the integrated validator client; vc still reports only a configured fee recipient
- Count cached slots in the own beacon committee members metric
- List what --publish-to-every-node covers
- Log a beacon node's failure to report genesis at debug
- Correct the archiver retry comment

title: Accept comma-separated and repeated list query parameters for blobs and sidecars
body:
Closes #1017

## Problem

`GET /eth/v1/beacon/blobs/{block_id}` only accepted `versioned_hashes` as repeated keys (`?versioned_hashes=0xa&versioned_hashes=0xb`). Clients that send a comma-separated list (`?versioned_hashes=0xa,0xb`), such as the Base node's L1 blob fetcher, got `invalid query string`. Other clients accept both forms, and Grandine already does for `id`, `status` and `topics`.

`indices` on `/eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/{block_id}` and `/eth/v1/debug/beacon/data_column_sidecars/{block_id}` had the same limitation.

## Change

- Added `deserialize_comma_separated_or_repeated`, which reads the values as strings, splits each on `,` and parses them with `FromStr`. It accepts `?k=a,b`, `?k=a&k=b`, and mixtures like `?k=a&k=b,c`.
- Used it for `BlobsQuery.versioned_hashes`, `BlobSidecarsQuery.indices` and `DataColumnSidecarsQuery.indices`. These fields are now `Vec` with `#[serde(default)]`. An empty list still means "all", as `None` did before.
- `serde_aux::field_attributes::deserialize_vec_from_string_or_vec` isn't used here because it rejects repeated numeric keys: they're buffered as strings, and `u64` won't deserialize from those.

## Testing

Added `test_deserialize_blobs_query` and `test_deserialize_indices_queries`. They go through the real `EthQuery` extractor and cover the empty, single, comma-separated, repeated and mixed forms. `cargo test -p http_api --features bls/blst,kzg_utils/blst --lib`: 36 passed.

title: Keep fallback execution clients updated
body:
Related to #998.

Forward newPayload and forkchoiceUpdated updates to fallback ELs even when the preferred EL succeeds.

## Changes

- Serialize updates per endpoint and retain only the latest pending background payload and forkchoice updates.
- Try another EL after SYNCING or an ACCEPTED newPayload response. Return the first definitive response, including INVALID, or the first provisional response if none is definitive.
- Omit payload attributes from background forkchoiceUpdated requests to avoid unnecessary builds.
- Bind payload IDs to their issuing endpoint and retry payload preparation once if retrieval fails.

Only the selected response is forwarded to the controller.

## Validation

- Passed 50 API/queue tests and 3 producer/controller tests, including existing tests.
- Verified synchronization and recovery with two Geth instances, including a SYNCING preferred EL and a VALID fallback.

Lagging ELs still rely on peer sync for missing ancestors. No overall proposal deadline is introduced.
